answer: Each identity claims one jetty pile serving a lagoon garden plot and locks a 70-credit bond on its serial. Each epoch it files a key-signed sounding of scour and lagoon level. An auditor recomputes scour from the lagoon bed-profile table, allowing 3% error; a miss, reused serial or missing filing burns the bond. First costs 34; the k-th 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6028 and 1000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-pile ring fails: the pile carries its owner's serial, so a second key filing it is rejected and both burn. An honest garden keeper pays 34 once, bond recovered.
